title: The roof after Book 10
question: Book 10 landed at 18:15. What did the last two days teach us about how we work, and what should Saturday's round chase instead of Q11?
serves: North star 3 (extraordinary) and Commandments I, II, IX; Investment Strategy (the IPS's 'balance growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, and financial flexibility')
essence: We argued over whether to keep fixing sentences or answer the questions Wharton actually asks.

We decided Saturday goes to one big question, why not a safe ladder and the rest in stocks, because two of six mock judges put that plan first and our draft never answers it; and every vote now waits until we've read Caplet's latest message.
So the next draft can gain a whole idea instead of another trim.
decided: 3-0: round 4 (Sat 31 Oct) asks why the gift's money sits in a Treasury floor from 2028 instead of stocks locked down in 2031 (the A09 rival); Q11 rides second
3-0: the $85,000 line is stale (V25's design), not wrong; already routed to the Window's Sat 31 audit, so no scout spends time on it
3-0: LS-06 broken a second time (the Long Room voted at 18:20 without reading Book 10, 18:15); goes to Sunday's review as a vote-gate rule
3-0: LS-12, a split panel earns a round only when the low judge's reason is one of Wharton's questions; the question sets the work, not the judge
seeds: Does V36's floor-from-2028 actually beat A09's lock-in-2031 on our own model paths, and what does it give up?
If it does, is that the paragraph-sized idea the next draft is missing for a growth-minded judge?
